page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor running at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core scaling and memory bandwidth present notable bottlenecks. Multi-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench falls into the average and weak categories respectively, while read-only memory bandwidth tests show weak throughput. Cryptographic workloads perform moderately, supported by hardware-accelerated instruction sets such as AES and SHA_NI.

The ecs.c8a.xlarge offers a cost-effective entry point for compute-focused workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local NVMe storage. Due to its weak multi-threaded decompression, database operations, and web serving throughput, it is less suited for high-concurrency web servers or heavy database hosting. Instead, the instance is best utilized for single-threaded processing tasks, lightweight batch processing, text processing, and utility workloads where dedicated CPU execution is required without high memory overhead.
